definition: RET is a human gene that encodes a receptor enzyme involved in signaling processes that affect the growth, movement, and development of neural cells. In psychology-related biological context, it refers to this neural-cell-related receptor protein rather than a counseling concept.

provenance.scope: Source record C18539; pinned source text

reasons: The definition adds an unsupported contrast to a “counseling concept,” which is not stated in the packet.
The packet supports RET as the human gene/protein RET and its role in neural-cell proliferation, migration, and differentiation, but the wording should stay within those supported claims only.
The definition claims RET is involved in “signaling processes,” but the packet only states roles in “proliferation, migration and differentiation of neural cells” and does not mention signaling.

Other parts of the definition (RET gene encoding a tyrosine-protein kinase receptor; involvement in neural cell proliferation/migration/differentiation, framed as growth/movement/development) are broadly consistent with the packet, but the unsupported “signaling processes” claim is substantive.
